transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Nora (Redwood AE), Mateo (Redwood SE), Lisa (Littleton CISO), Raj (Littleton PM), Simone (Eng Mgr)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a security-focused POC: confirm success criteria, workload sizing and benchmarks, timelines; deep dive on security/compliance (SOC 2 / ISO / SSO-SAML / RBAC / audit logs / KMS); decide hosted vs private options for pilot.

Topics:
- Success criteria and acceptance metrics for the pilot
- Workload sizing: RPS, concurrency, token lengths, throughput targets
- Benchmarks: latency (p50/p95), throughput, quality checks
- Security/compliance: SOC 2, ISO 27001, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logging, KMS, data residency
- Pilot timeline, deliverables and acceptance gating

Transcript:
[00:00] Nora: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll keep to the hour, quick intros?
[00:08] Lisa: lisa chen, ciso at littleton, hi.
[00:10] Raj: raj, product, focusing on clinical workflows.
[00:12] Simone: simone, eng manager, we'll be hands on for infra.
[00:15] Nora: great, from redwood mateo is our se, he'll walk benchmarks and infra.
[00:19] Mateo: hi all, quick agenda, scope success criteria, we need sizing, run a benchmark plan, and cover security questions.

[03:02] Raj: the high level: we want to pilot summarization + triage for inbound patient messages, expect around 30k messages/month in pilot, peaks to 12 rps, avg message length around 300 tokens, worst case 2k tokens for attachments. We're most sensitive to 95th latency for short messages, target p95 < 700ms.

[06:15] Mateo: ok that gives a good baseline. For peak 12 rps with 300 tokens we typically see hosted latency in the 200-400ms p50, p95 depends on batching and concurrency. For a fair benchmark we'll run both hosted and a dedicated pool; and we can also simulate a private VPC deployment if you need KMS and VPC controls.

[08:40] Lisa: security is the gating item. we require SOC 2 Type II, and are starting ISO 27001 scoping. also need SSO via SAML to integrate with okta, strict RBAC so only certain roles can call model endpoints, and full audit logs with immutable retention. can redwood provide tamper-evident logs and exportable audit trails?

[09:10] Nora: yes we can provide SOC 2 Type II report under nda, iso artifacts we can share the scope we cover, and SAML SSO is supported. audit logs are available through console and can be exported, mateo will confirm retention and immutability semantics.

[11:30] Mateo: quick caveat on exports: for hosted we provide tenant-level audit logs with event types (auth, request, model selection, response, admin actions) and retention options. for immutability/tamper-evidence we integrate with your SIEM via secure webhook / syslog; for the most strict controls we recommend Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) where logs stay in your cloud account.

[14:05] Lisa: encryption at rest and in transit is a must, plus bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with KMS/HSM integration. also we need clarity on PII handling: can data be excluded from model training and do you have dataplane segregation?

[14:40] Nora: we do not train models on customer data for hosted customers by default; we have a DPA and privacy terms, and for sensitive datasets we recommend dedicated or private deployments where data is isolated. BYOK with KMS is supported in private and for dedicated in some tiers, mateo can outline exact flows.

[16:55] Raj: for acceptance criteria beyond perf: summaries must achieve >= 85% accuracy on our evaluation set (we'll provide a holdout), no PII leakage in outputs, latency p95 under 700ms for standard messages, and audit logs ingested into our SIEM within 5 minutes.

[18:22] Mateo: good, we'll design the benchmark to capture end-to-end latency (request ingress, inference, postprocessing), plus a quality eval run against your holdout. we'll surface token costs and expected unit economics so you can compare hosted vs dedicated.

[20:40] Simone: from infra side we need to know concurrency limits, retry behavior, and how KV cache works for chat-like sessions. some transcription here: sometimes our notes say KV cash instead of KV cache.

[21:05] Mateo: right, KV cache helps warm the model for repeated contexts and reduces latency; we'll show the cache hit rates in benchmark outputs. concurrency and autoscale settings can be tuned but for the pilot we'll allocate a dedicated pool with predictable throughput to hit your p95 targets.

[24:00] Lisa: compliance questions: do you have SOC 2 audit authority and a scope listing? can we do a SOC 2 review as part of procurement? Also are you willing to sign our standard DPA and a security addendum?

[24:32] Nora: yes, we'll share a SOC 2 summary and cert under NDA, and we typically accept customer DPAs with minor redlines; we'll have legal engage. there's a standard security addendum we can attach.

[27:10] Raj: timeline: we want a 4-week pilot. week 1 security review + infra spin up, week 2 benchmark and eval runs, week 3 iterate on model configs and prompts, week 4 acceptance and final report. is that realistic?

[27:45] Mateo: yes that's a typical cadence. we may need 3-5 business days to spin up a private VPC or dedicated pool depending on procurement. If you choose hosted, spin up is faster but you lose some controls.

[29:50] Lisa: procurement note: we need proof of encryption keys control, policy docs, and personnel access lists. can you provide RBAC controls like role templates and admin separation?

[30:22] Nora: yes RBAC and SSO/SAML with groups from Okta. role templates include viewer, developer, admin, and security-audit-only. we can lock certain roles to only view logs and not export.

[33:10] Simone: how granular are logs? we need request-level logs with request id, model version, prompt hash (or anonymized), response size, user id, and timestamp. also we want an export endpoint or SIEM integration.

[33:45] Mateo: we emit request-level events and can include model version and request id; for prompts we can provide prompt hashes and anonymization options in the audit logs. SIEM integration via secure transfer or cloud logging is supported.

[36:00] Raj: on the benchmarks - what tooling will you run? will it simulate our message distribution and token length distribution?

[36:28] Mateo: yes we'll use a reproducible harness (k6-jobs + internal runner) with your sample dataset distribution. benchmark outputs: p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rates, and quality evals against your holdout. we'll also run a degradation test to exercise fallbacks and model variant routing.

[38:10] Lisa: any third-party attestations beyond SOC2? we mentioned ISO 27001 earlier - what's your timeline for cert?

[38:30] Nora: we are working through ISO scoping; we don't have full cert yet but can share our controls and the scope. if ISO is a hard requirement for production we can discuss a private deployment or contractual mitigations during the pilot.

[41:00] Raj: what's the difference in unit economics between hosted and dedicated? rough numbers are fine.

[41:23] Mateo: rough: hosted is easiest but higher per-token costs; dedicated reduces unit cost by ~30-50% depending on utilization. we will include modeled cost projections for your traffic profile as part of the benchmark deliverable.

[44:12] Lisa: legal/security will want to see retention knobs and the ability to purge data on demand. do you support deletion APIs and proof of deletion?

[44:35] Mateo: yes we have deletion APIs and logs of deletion actions; for private deployments deletions are under your control. for hosted we can perform purge and provide audit evidence.

[47:00] Simone: network architecture question: for private can we use VPC peering, private link, or on-prem?

[47:25] Nora: private supports VPC peering and private link; on-prem option is available for air-gapped environments but is a longer procurement.

[49:40] Raj: acceptance gating recap: performance (p95 < 700ms), quality (>=85% on holdout), security docs signed, SAML SSO + RBAC enabled, audit logs flowing to SIEM.

[50:05] Nora: yep that's our mutual checklist. we'll produce a POC runbook and benchmark plan.

[51:10] Lisa: small note, sometimes transcripts read sam-el for saml which is confusing in notes, but ok.

[51:30] Nora: ha yeah, transcription quirks. final logistics: we'll send SOC2 under NDA, mateo will send benchmark plan and scripts, and we'll aim to run benchmarks week of 2027-08-23.

[53:00] Raj: estimated sign-off mid-September if pilot goes well.

[54:12] Nora: perfect, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window and attach the security artifacts. thanks all.

[55:00] Lisa: thanks, bye.
